proposals: The Department of Fertilisers should publish a monthly table giving, for urea and DAP, the import-parity price, the subsidy paid per tonne and the farmer retail price side by side, so the share of a global price shock the subsidy absorbs is measured directly rather than inferred from a nearly flat WPI line.

The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices should publish, alongside its projected cost of production, an in-year update of actual fertiliser and diesel costs per hectare, so a squeeze like the 2021–23 fertiliser shock shows up in an official series while it is happening, not after.

The Department of Consumer Affairs should publish the monthly landed import price of the main edible oils alongside their retail prices, so the near one-to-one global pass-through into CPI oils and fats, which swung from -18.17% in June 2023 to +21.24% in August 2025, can be traced month by month.
